compensating.why: hop 2 places the units digit of the leading limb one decade higher
hop 3 asks for the exponent of ten times the digit, less one
hop 4 asks for the exponent of the digit below x (at most instead of below)

context_edits.old: /** Compute natural logarithm of a derivative structure.

edits.old: return limb > FastMath.pow(10, decade + 1) ? decade + 1 : decade;

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the decimal exponent of the most significant limb: hop 1 selects that limb, hop 2 adds the placement 4 (exponent - 1) of the limb's units digit, and hops 3 and 4 pass the limb along. The gold's javadoc promises the exponent of the greatest power of ten below the limb; for the limb 12 that is 1 (10 < 12), and the variant returns 0, while it returns the right value 3 for the limb 1234, so no uniform change at a caller repairs the trigger. The convention is pinned outside the gold: DfpDec.round counts the decimal digits of the most significant limb exactly, Dfp.dfp2sci finds the first non-zero decimal digit of the mantissa digit by digit, and Dfp.power10 places 10^e with the limb exponent e / 4 + 1 and the leading limb 10^(e mod 4), the inverse of the chain's placement; DfpTest::testPower10, DfpDecTest::testRound and DfpTest::testToString pass, and DfpDecTest::testNextAfter passes through the chain on limbs where the gold's result is exact.
